points.description: Seasonality: regular oscillating variations in monthly/seasonal hydrologic events, caused by the earth's rotation (revolution) around the sun.
points.partial_credit: Half if it says seasonal/periodic regular variation but gives no cause (earth around sun), or gives cause only vaguely.

points.description: Long-term oscillations: oscillations about the trend line occurring over very large periods of time (much longer than seasonal), well distributed about their mean value.
points.partial_credit: Half if it only says they occur over a long time without reference to the trend/mean or the contrast with seasonal cycles.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both ideas: seasonality is regular, short-period (monthly/seasonal) variation due to earth's motion around the sun, and long-term oscillations occur over very long periods about the trend line/mean. Give part marks for a vague or incomplete statement of either idea. A wrong statement on one side loses only that point; a student who names only one type earns at most 1 mark.
